chunks: My father narrated to us, may God be pleased with him, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to us, from Al-Hussein ibn Ishaq the merchant, from Ali ibn Mahzyar, from Hammad ibn Isa and Fuzalat, from Muawiyah ibn Ammar, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the Takbir on the days of Tashriq for the people of the cities (non-Mina residents), so he said: On the Day of Sacrifice, [it is] after the Dhuhr prayer until the completion of ten prayers, and for the people of Mina, fifteen prayers. If he stays until Dhuhr and Asr, he says Takbir.

key_terms.أَهْلَ مِنًى: The people of Mina, referring to pilgrims staying in the Mina camp
key_terms.أَيَّامَ التَّشْرِيقِ: The days of Tashriq (11th-13th Dhu al-Hijjah) following Eid al-Adha
key_terms.التَّكْبِير: Takbir (saying 'Allahu Akbar'), a ritual declaration of God's greatness
key_terms.يَوْمَ النَّحْرِ: The Day of Sacrifice (Eid al-Adha, 10th Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling and duration of Takbir during the days of Tashriq for Hajj pilgrims according to Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal* details the specific jurisprudence of the Takbir al-Tashriq, distinguishing between the ten prayers for pilgrims in Mina and the five for those in other cities, reflecting the distinct ritual statuses of the Hajj sites. It highlights the scholarly emphasis on precise liturgical timing and the flexibility for those who extend their stay in Mina, underscoring the practical application of Prophetic traditions in Shia fiqh. The ruling connects the physical act of pilgrimage with the spiritual affirmation of God’s greatness, a core theme in the Hajj narrative.
